Since it's internal, this isn't really a case for the license/assurance-boundary skill — that's about public-facing claims. Just a wording fix.

The issue with "guaranteed to never fail, 100% thread-safe in all cases" is it's an absolute claim that's hard to actually back up — what happens if the input is malformed, or under some untested concurrency pattern? A reviewer (or future you debugging a weird race) will trust it and skip checking.

A more defensible version, tied to what's actually true of the implementation:

```
// Thread-safe: uses only atomic operations / immutable state, no shared mutable data.
// Errors are caught internally and returned via the result type rather than thrown.
```

Adjust the specifics to match the actual mechanism (lock-free, mutex-guarded, immutable, etc.) rather than asserting the property alone — that's what makes it verifiable instead of aspirational.

If you tell me what the function actually does for thread-safety and error handling, I can tighten the wording further.
